verdicts.reading: Majority agreed: by 2014 telework and home-schooling expand and the work/leisure boundary diminishes significantly, sharply altering family dynamics.
verdicts.reason: The view is not only a value judgment: telework expansion and work spilling into non-work time are measured. Both moved in the stated direction but modestly: ATUS share doing some work at home on workdays rose 19% (2003) to 23% (2014), and Pew 2014 found 35% of online workers say technology increased their hours. A real but minority blurring, not a significant erosion; 'sharply alter family dynamics' has no measure and is not graded. Held in part. Grader A's ungradable discards the measurable half.

evidence.title: BLS American Time Use Survey 2014
evidence.shows: 23% of employed did some or all work at home on days worked in 2014 vs 19% in 2003.

evidence.title: Pew Research: Technology's Impact on Workers
evidence.shows: 35% of online workers say internet/email/phones increased hours worked; 39% say more flexibility.

verdicts.reading: Majority agreed: by 2014 zealot groups in politics, religion and violence solidify and grow in number, helped by online networks (global, as worded).
verdicts.reason: The statement has no geographic limit, so the global reading dominates. RAND (2014) counted Salafi-jihadist groups rising 58% (31 to 49) 2010-2013 with fighters more than doubling, and ISIS drew tens of thousands of foreign fighters largely via online propaganda by 2014-15. Grader B's SPLC count of US hate groups (784 in 2014) is a US formal-group measure; SPLC itself attributes the drop to migration online, which fits the 'networks flourish online' clause rather than refuting growth.

evidence.title: PolitiFact on RAND 'A Persistent Threat' (2014)
evidence.shows: RAND: Salafi-jihadist groups rose 58%, from 31 (2010) to 49 (2013); fighters more than doubled.

evidence.title: Foreign fighters in the Syrian civil war and War in Iraq (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Soufan Group: 27,000-31,000 foreign fighters by late 2015; online recruitment role.

evidence.title: SPLC: The Year in Hate and Extremism
evidence.shows: US hate groups fell to 784 in 2014; activity shifted online (counter-evidence for US formal groups only).

verdicts.reading: Majority agreed: by 2014 internet use enlarges social networks and this enhances trust in society.
verdicts.reason: The forecast's payoff, and the reason the statement exists, is higher social trust; network growth is the stated mechanism. Trust fell: GSS 'most people can be trusted' about 34% in 2018-2024, below mid-2000s GSS levels, and 71% of Americans in 2019 said interpersonal trust had declined. The consequence failed, so the view misses. Grader B's baseline is a reading error: the 44-45% figure for 2006 is from Pew's own 2006 survey, not the GSS, so the 44%-to-34% drop compares two different surveys (direction still holds on GSS alone).

evidence.title: Pew Research: Americans' Trust in One Another
evidence.shows: GSS share saying most people can be trusted fell from 46% (1972) to 34% (2018-2024).

evidence.title: Pew Research: Trust and Distrust in America
evidence.shows: 71% say interpersonal trust declined over the past 20 years.

evidence.title: Pew Research: Americans and Social Trust
evidence.shows: 45% 'most people can be trusted' is from Pew's own Oct-Nov 2006 survey, not the GSS.

verdicts.reading: Majority disagreed: by 2014 most people will not filter out challenging political views online, and political discourse will not be further polarized that way.
verdicts.reason: The statement's headline is further polarization; filtering is its mechanism. The majority's rejection held on filtering: only about 21% of Americans were consistent ideologues with insulated media diets in 2014. It failed on polarization: partisan antipathy more than doubled 1994-2014 and the most polarized were also the most filtered. Grader A's hit grades only the 'most people filter' clause and drops the polarization clause the respondents also rejected.

evidence.title: Pew Research: Political Polarization in the American Public
evidence.shows: Consistent ideologues 10% to 21% (a minority); very unfavorable views of the other party roughly doubled 1994-2014.

evidence.title: Pew Research: Political Polarization & Media Habits
evidence.shows: Most Americans have mixed views and varied sources; consistent ideologues cluster in insulated outlets.

verdicts.reading: Majority disagreed: by 2020 intelligent agents will not cut humans so completely out of key activities (surveillance, security, tracking) that unrecognized dangers become irreversible.
verdicts.reason: The defining content of the rejected scenario is dangers 'not recognized until it is impossible to reverse them', which has no public measure. Grader B graded a narrower proxy (autonomous weapons) that the text does not name; for the named activities, fully automated pipelines did exist by 2020 (algorithmic mass surveillance, automated trading and content filtering), so even the proxy does not clearly support a hit. Looked for incident databases; they record recognized harms only.

evidence.title: AI Incident Database
evidence.shows: Indexes realized, reported AI harms; no measure of unrecognized or irreversible dependencies.

evidence.title: Lethal autonomous weapon (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Weapons were mostly human-supervised by 2020; a proxy, not the surveillance/tracking activities named.

verdicts.reading: Majority agreed: in 2020 the mobile phone is the primary internet connection, and the only one, for a majority of the world's people.
verdicts.reason: Text says 'the only one for a majority of the people across the world'. Primary held: 92% of 4.54B internet users connected via mobile and mobile broadband (75 per 100) far exceeded fixed (about 15 per 100). 'Only one for a majority of the world' did not: only about 51-58% of the world was online at all, and three-quarters of users 16-64 also used computers, so mobile-only users were well under half the world's population. Grader A's reading drops the 'only one' clause.

evidence.title: ITU: Measuring digital development, Facts and figures 2020
evidence.shows: Mobile broadband 75 per 100 inhabitants vs far lower fixed broadband; just over half the world online.

evidence.title: DataReportal: Digital 2020 Global Overview
evidence.shows: 4.54B internet users; 92% connect via mobile; three-quarters of users 16-64 also use laptops/desktops.

verdicts.reading: Majority agreed: in 2020 well-connected knowledge workers in developed nations have eliminated the boundary between work hours and personal time, with work and play integrated in most of their lives; net positive.
verdicts.reason: The boundary claim is measurable even though 'net positive' is not (not graded). In 2020, 71% of telework-capable US workers worked from home all or most of the time and 49% of new teleworkers had more freedom over hours, so boundaries blurred widely; but it was pandemic-forced, not willing, only 38% found work-life balance easier, and right-to-disconnect laws (France 2017 onward) show boundaries were being restored, not erased. Held in part. Same treatment as 2005-004.

evidence.title: Pew Research: How the coronavirus outbreak has changed the way Americans work
evidence.shows: 71% of telework-capable workers home all/most of the time (20% pre-pandemic); 49% more hour flexibility; 38% balance easier.

evidence.title: Right to disconnect (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Laws restoring work/personal boundaries: France 2017, Ontario and Slovakia 2021.

verdicts.reading: Majority chose: by 2020 it will be clear that the internet has improved reading, writing and the rendering of knowledge.
verdicts.reason: A causal judgment about the internet's net effect on three things; no public measure isolates it. Indicators point both ways: NAEP reading scores declined from 2015 (against), while the volume of writing and open reference works such as Wikipedia grew (for 'rendering of knowledge'). Grader B graded only test-score literacy and dropped 'rendering of knowledge'; NAEP cannot attribute the decline to internet use. Looked for NAEP and literacy trend data.

evidence.title: National Assessment of Educational Progress (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: NAEP scores declined from 2015 onward; no attribution to internet use.

evidence.title: NAEP 2019 Reading Highlights
evidence.shows: Official 2019 reading results, grades 4 and 8.

verdicts.reading: Majority chose: the hot gadgets and applications of 2020 will often come out of the blue, unanticipated by 2010's savviest innovators.
verdicts.reason: Both graders agree no verdict is possible; the question is which non-verdict. D16 unfalsifiable requires readings that each give a verdict. Here neither the product reading nor the category reading can be scored, because no public record exists of what 2010's 'savviest innovators' anticipated, and 'often' has no count. That is D22 ungradable. Looked for: a record of 2010 innovator expectations against 2020 hit products.

evidence.title: TikTok (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Launched 2016; about 800M MAU by July 2020; one 2020 hit, no measure of whether it was anticipated.

verdicts.reading: Majority chose: in 2020 hyperconnected young people do not suffer notable cognitive shortcomings when multitasking, and the cognitive changes are positive overall.
verdicts.reason: Not only a value judgment: the scenario makes a specific factual claim ('they do not suffer notable cognitive shortcomings as they multitask'), and the research record by 2018 went against it: heavy media multitaskers perform worse in several cognitive domains (Ophir 2009; Uncapher and Wagner 2018 review), consistent with option B's 'distracted, do not retain'. The review calls causation inconclusive, but the claim concerns shortcomings, not their cause. 'Wired differently' and 'positive overall' are not graded. Low confidence.

evidence.title: Media multitasking (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Uncapher & Wagner 2018: heavy media multitaskers have worse performance in several cognitive domains; literature sparse and inconclusive on causation.

verdicts.reading: Majority chose: by 2020 most people pay by smart device, so cash and cards have mostly disappeared from transactions in advanced countries.
verdicts.reason: An adoption claim under D16 plus a displacement state. Mobile payment reached a measurable share: 46% of US consumers made at least one mobile payment in the 12 months to Oct 2020 (38% in 2019). The displacement failed: cash, debit and credit still made about three-quarters of US payments (19%, 28%, 27%). Adoption grew well past 5% while the stated end-state did not arrive, which is a partial, not a miss. Grader A's 'roughly a quarter' adoption figure was unsourced; the Fed figure is 46% for any mobile payment.

evidence.title: Atlanta Fed: 2020 Survey of Consumer Payment Choice
evidence.shows: 46% of consumers made at least one mobile payment in the 12 months to Oct 2020, up from 38% in 2019.

evidence.title: Federal Reserve: 2021 Findings from the Diary of Consumer Payment Choice
evidence.shows: 2020: cash 19%, debit 28%, credit 27% of US consumer payments.

verdicts.reading: Majority chose: by 2020 human and machine analysis of large data sets improves social, political and economic intelligence (e.g. nowcasting); the 'huge positive' clause is a value judgment and is not graded.
verdicts.reason: Both graders agree the measurable clause held: central banks routinely publish big-data nowcasts (Atlanta Fed GDPNow from 2014, NY Fed nowcast) with alternative-data and ML inputs. Under D22/D27 an unmeasurable clause is not graded; it cannot count against the view. Grader A downgraded to partial for the ungraded value clause, which mixes the two rules. Note: the factual clause is shared by option B, so the hit says little about the panel's real split.

evidence.title: Nowcasting (economics) (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Central banks primary users; GDPNow (2014) and NY Fed nowcast published routinely; social media and ML inputs added.

verdicts.reading: Majority answered yes: by 2025 a major cyber attack has caused widespread harm to a nation's security, defined as significant loss of life or losses at the level of tens of billions of dollars.
verdicts.reason: Read 'at the levels of tens of billions' as an order of magnitude, the dominant reading of a definitional threshold. NotPetya (2017), a Russian military operation, disabled Ukrainian ministries, banks, metro, energy and telecoms and caused over $10B in damage per the White House. That meets both the national-security and the scale test, at the lower edge. Grader B's partial rests on reading 'tens' as at least $20B; defensible but the narrower reading.

evidence.title: 2017 Ukraine ransomware attacks (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: NotPetya: over $10B total damage (White House); Ukrainian ministries, banks, metro, energy, telecoms hit; attributed to GRU.

verdicts.reading: Majority chose: changes set in motion by COVID-19 make life in 2025 mostly worse for most people than it was when the pandemic began.
verdicts.reason: The option is an explicit comparison with early 2020, not a counterfactual (the counterfactual is the third option), so it is measurable on population-level wellbeing. Global HDI hit a record high in 2023 and kept rising; Gallup's 2024 global thriving median (33%) is higher than before the pandemic and suffering (7%) matches the record low. Life was not mostly worse for most people. Uneven recovery in about half of LDCs affects a minority of people.

evidence.title: Gallup: More People Globally Living Better Lives
evidence.shows: 2024: median 33% thriving across 142 countries, above pre-pandemic levels; suffering 7%, matching record low.

evidence.title: UN News: 'Record high' in UN development index masks stark disparities
evidence.shows: Global HDI projected at record high in 2023; all OECD countries above 2019; 18 of 35 declining LDCs not recovered.
